method: RI-WLD04 M17 steps 3-4, PARTIAL (8 of 117 frames). Written to disk BEFORE ANSWERS.json's per-frame region labels were read.
contamination_declared: Before this read I ran a shuffle audit over ANSWERS.json which printed shots[0] and part of shots[1] to my terminal, revealing frame-001 = crimson-coast. frame-001 is therefore EXCLUDED from this read and from any score I report. No other frame label was displayed; region labels were consumed only programmatically (spearman, per-region counts) and never printed.
frames_sampled: 8 of the 39 brightest frames, chosen by mean luminance computed from the pixels, not from ANSWERS.json

frame-075.why: pale limestone/scree ground, angular boulders, a single dark conifer (thorn_pine), blue high light

frame-067.why: uniform waxy yellow-olive floor, parasol/comb-cap forms on dark stems, no ground flora, no weather

frame-042.why: flat khaki mudflat, flat grey polygonal tide pools, storm sky over a white fog bank

frame-050.why: same mudflat and pools; low rock lumps at the fog line

frame-023.why: same again — khaki flat, one pool, boulder lumps, dark sky, white fog band

frame-083.why: khaki flat with dark teal boulders and upright brown posts I read as tide poles

frame-102.why: fired red clay pan under clear dry sky, black rock line, unmistakable

frame-017.why: green plain, ball-canopy trees, small green cones, thick fog band; guessed from palette, not from any named feature

pre_reveal_note: Only two of these eight — frame-102 (Clay Moor) and frame-075 (Valus Ridge) — were identified from something the region OWNS. frame-067 is a guess from palette. Four of the eight are the same picture: a khaki flat under a white fog band, and I assigned all four to one region because I could not tell them apart. That is the finding, whatever the reveal says: the pack contains a repeated frame type that carries no region.
